Name: EV1 Rear (DoubleWishbone stand-in; real EV1 rear is a 5-link beam axle)
//PROVENANCE: Read this before treating any number in this file as an EV1 measurement.
THE TOPOLOGY IS WRONG HERE. The EV1 has no independent rear suspension: no
control arms, no uprights, no tie rods. EV1 chassis manual, printed page 271:
'The rear suspension on the EV1 consists of a rear axle assembly with aluminum
end castings and a tubular center section. There are two coil springs, two twin
tube shock absorbers and five connecting links with non-replaceable bushings.
These five connecting links are composed of two upper suspension leading links,
two lower suspension trailing links, and a track bar.' That is a one-piece beam
axle located by five links, so no EV1 part corresponds to any hardpoint below.
Chrono's JSON factory does offer closer templates - SolidAxle carries the same
link set but is a steered axle, and GenericWheeledSuspension could express the
layout exactly - but neither can be filled in without hardpoints, and none are
published. See docs/TODO.md. Until then this file is a stand-in whose roll and
pitch response is plausible and whose kinematics are not the EV1's.
